english_draft: Microsoft reported Q2 FY2026 results for the quarter ended December 31, 2025. Total revenue was $81.3 billion, up 17% (15% in constant currency). GAAP operating income was $38.3 billion, up 21% (19% in constant currency). GAAP net income was $38.5 billion, up 60%, mainly due to a $7.6 billion net gain from investments in OpenAI. Non-GAAP net income was $30.9 billion, up 23% (21% in constant currency). GAAP diluted EPS was $5.16; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $4.14. Microsoft Cloud revenue was $51.5 billion, up 26% (24% in constant currency). Commercial remaining performance obligation reached $625 billion, up 110%. Segment revenue: Productivity and Business Processes $34.1 billion, up 16%; Intelligent Cloud $32.9 billion, up 29%; More Personal Computing $14.3 billion, down 3%. Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 39% (38% in constant currency). Windows OEM and Devices revenue increased 1% (flat in constant currency). Xbox content and services revenue decreased 5% (6% in constant currency). Microsoft returned $12.7 billion to shareholders in dividends and share repurchases, up 32%. No pre-earnings Preview article was available in the supplied sources; hence this Analysis cannot compare with a contemporaneous preview.
reader_questions: Why did GAAP net income grow 60% while non-GAAP net income grew only 23%?
Why did commercial remaining performance obligation jump 110% to $625 billion?
How did the More Personal Computing segment decline despite Azure growth of 39%?

Fact: GAAP net income $38.5 billion, up 60%; non-GAAP net income $30.9 billion, up 23% (21% cc). Source: opening bullet and Non-GAAP table.
Fact: GAAP diluted EPS $5.16; non-GAAP diluted EPS $4.14. Source: opening bullet and reconciliation table.

Fact: The gap between GAAP and non-GAAP net income is the OpenAI investment impact: net gain $7.6 billion / $1.02 per share in Q2 FY2026, versus net loss $939 million / $0.12 in Q2 FY2025. Source: Non-GAAP Definition.
